structured_output.summary: Attempt 2 is a genuinely additive, mechanically verified overlay. All four attempt-1 lows are fixed: verify_typescript035_source.py now proves 16 reused declarations (transitive closure) span-exact with four mutation variants each; the new graph nodes carry inputPresence/inputNull; the oracle grew 376→906 cases with nested wrong-type/null corners; the generator import moved to the header. I independently confirmed node reuse (s009590 optional bool, s009601 optional string), that exactly six frozen exports reference the 12-node clone closure, upstream field shapes in the pinned 0.35.0 file, lossless typed-wins projection in generated.rs, the 23-default denominator with a separately recorded alias, and that all 107 recorded checks exit 0 on the reviewed SHA, including both compilers. One low hardening gap: the two new upstream schema declarations are hand-transcribed, not span-pinned.

findings.description: ContentTypeConfiguration/ContentTypeConfigurations node shapes (the four protection keys, the four direction keys, optionality and passthrough) are hand-transcribed in Python. verify_reused_profile_declarations only span-pins declarations that exist in the frozen 0.34.0 inventory, so these two genuinely new upstream declarations are covered solely by the whole-file manifest hash. At the current pin the transcription is correct (I verified contracts/sources/typescript-0.35.0/src/models/mgmt-security-profile.ts:239-269). The oracle/Rust replay would not catch a future fifth typed key, because its field cases are generated from the same hand-list (tools/typescript035-oracle.mts:67,73), and Rust would silently treat the key as passthrough.
findings.required_fix: Pin the two new declarations' exact text/sha256 in verify_typescript035_source.py (same span technique as the reused closure) and derive or assert the overlay's property key sets from that pinned text, so a re-pin that changes either new schema fails before generation.

evidence: Closure and root completeness: tools/typescript035_profiles.py:77-85 derives the ancestor closure from the four projected sids and raises unless it equals the 12 reviewed clones. I independently grepped contracts/typescript.json for export-level refs (8-space indent) to all 12 clone sids and found exactly six: s009588 (:155247), s009599 (:42444), s009606 (:176475), s009612 (:207633), s009632 (:52658), s009651 (:207590) — so the six registered typescript:0.35.0: roots are the complete affected export set and the other six clones are internal wrappers.

Type reuse verified against the frozen inventory and pinned source: s009588 catchall s009589 is ZodNever with passthrough and the four protection props s009593/4/5/7 (contracts/typescript.json:347496-347546); s009590 is ZodOptional<ZodBoolean> (:347550) and s009601 ZodOptional<ZodString> (:347641), matching upstream 'enable-full-conversation-inspection': z.boolean().optional() (mgmt-security-profile.ts:276), 'content-type-mode' (:288) and dlp_tenant_id (:334, :368). ModelConfigurationSchema = ContentTypeConfigurationSchema.extend (:272), which is why copying s009588's four protection properties is the exact upstream shape.

Attempt-1 finding 1 resolved: tools/verify_typescript035_source.py:48-84 locates each reused declaration by its unique 'export const' anchor, compares the frozen text at exact length plus terminating semicolon, re-hashes it, and expands transitively over \w*Schema references. tools/test_typescript035_source.py:31-58 asserts the resulting closure is exactly 16 names and, for each, that a nullable insertion, an appended .optional(), a duplicate declaration and a deletion all fail, that a tampered inventory sha256 fails, and that line shifts are harmless.

Attempt-1 finding 2 resolved: tools/typescript035_profiles.py:98-105 emits inputPresence 'accepts'/inputNull 'rejects' on both the protection and direction properties; tools/test_typescript035_profiles.py:114-135 asserts the metadata, the passthrough/catchall reuse of s009589, the exact key sets, and that no new node carries vendorProjection.

Attempt-1 finding 3 resolved: tools/typescript035-oracle.mts:107-162 adds 36 nested mutation paths (6 wrong-type/null values each) plus latency cases for both ContentTypeConfigurationSchema and ModelConfigurationSchema. Recorded run: {"roots":8,"cases":906,"accepted":231} exit 0 (checks.json:2911) versus 376 at attempt 1, with tsc --strict exit 0 (:2949). tools/test_typescript035_oracle.py:54-67 pins specific nested rejections independently.
Attempt-1 finding 4 resolved: tools/generate_validation.py:14 imports default_aliases in the header block.

Oracle integrity and isolation: tools/typescript035-oracle.mts:19 runs the source verifier before any copy, :22-25 pins Zod to the committed lockfile, :34 replaces the DLP identifier with placeholder '100', :194-225 executes in a disposable .local workspace and removes it. I confirmed the real upstream identifier 8259670718644550000 appears only in the pinned fixture, the verifier and historical phase-26 records — never in contracts/typescript-035-oracle.json. tools/test_typescript035_oracle.py:73-105 proves tampered source/manifest fail before execution (no UPSTREAM_EXECUTED marker, no workspace) and that stale corpora or a changed script fail without rewriting bytes.

Rust/TypeScript equivalence is executed, not asserted: crates/scm-sdk/tests/typescript035_models.rs:44-87 replays every one of the 906 cases through validation::parse (versioned roots for the six, plain names for the two new schemas), compares acceptance and normalized output, typed-round-trips each root back to the Zod output, and requires at least one acceptance and one rejection per root. This test runs under feature management (crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:21 management = ["models", "dlp"]) and both recorded management runs executed cargo test and the directional_profiles example at exit 0 on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 (checks.json:2981, :3013).

Lossless additive projection uses the pre-existing mechanism (tools/generate_models.py:471-506): generated.rs:4467-4512, :14527-14578 and :153641-153652 remove the projected key and retain an undecodable value as an extension; :4549-4556, :14638 and :153731-153737 skip a same-key extension only when the typed field is set; KNOWN excludes projection keys so baseline collision errors are not globally weakened. Both new types keep derive(Deserialize) with flattened extensions (generated.rs:13370-13383, :13491-13504) and expose SCHEMA/parse/builder/build_validated.

Default alias is bounded and exercised: tools/generate_validation.py:146-155 refuses an alias whose original is not exactly {binding: default, default: []}; tools/response_defaults.py:69-79,117-120 re-checks the alias root and field and still asserts the 23-binding denominator, recording it in contracts/response-defaults.json:498-506 separately; crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/tests.rs:209-220 asserts semantics.len()==70 with [] inserted and omitted under ResponseWithoutDefaults; crates/scm-sdk/tests/typescript035_models.rs:198-213 covers Request/Response/ResponseWithoutDefaults for the versioned list root.

Determinism and frozen-byte preservation: tools/typescript035_profiles.py:218-233 (--check) reconstructs the committed graph from the committed graph minus the overlay, and re-derives the parity ledger and native-models supplemental keys; generate_models.py:1049-1126 regenerates graph, Rust and ledgers through the same Overlay. tools/test_typescript035_implementation.py:25-53 proves contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json differs from baseline 578f2e6 only in provenance.generatorSha256 and model-regressions.json only in provenance.sha256/oracleSha256, each bound to current bytes; :112-148 proves every historical graph node/root survives unchanged, that added nodes/roots are exactly the 12 clones plus 4 new nodes and 8 roots, and that native-models schemas/modelExports/unionVariantPins/aliases are byte-equal to baseline.

Check evidence: docs/reviews/phase-27-chunk-models-and-validation-attempt-02.checks.json records source_sha256 cfc54942... matching the reviewed SHA, source_unchanged true, passed true, and 107 checks with no exit_code other than 0, no timeout true and no source_unchanged false. The set matches tools/check_phase.py:317-353 (phase-23 cumulative minus package-archive checks, every tools/test_*.py suite individually, the five new 0.35.0 commands, dependency audit reordered before the Rust matrix, management feature set on both compilers).

Narrow, documented oracle adapter change: tools/schema-oracle.mts:242-249 keeps the original discriminator map and adapts only mapped children; request schemas untouched. tools/test_schema_oracle.py:12-48 executes the extracted adapter across two distinct Zod module identities, proves the old z.discriminatedUnion rebuild throws, and checks dispatch, enum widening, unknown-key passthrough and each rejection case.
limitations: Read-only Read/Glob/Grep only: I could not recompute the SHA-256 of the reviewed source or of the checks artifact, nor re-execute any check or test. Pass/fail conclusions rest on the recorded commands, exit codes, stdout and executed_at values cross-read against tools/check_phase.py:317-353.
I did not read credential or tenant-registration files, used no .local/typescript checkout, and made no network calls.

The oracle-to-Rust comparison is Mode::Request only; the new versioned roots' Response/ResponseWithoutDefaults behavior is not compared case-by-case against Zod. This matches the plan's deliberate retention of frozen tolerant response validation, and the one defaulted field is covered in all three modes, but it bounds what the 906-case replay proves.

schema_graph.json and semantics.json are single-line minified artifacts; I verified their new content through targeted greps, the generator reconstruction path and the Python/Rust regressions rather than end-to-end reading.

Phase 27 deliberately omits the clean extracted package-consumer checks (tools/check_phase.py:323, deferred to phase 28), so milestone 2's package-consumer wording is only partly satisfied here; check_phase.py belongs to the wire-and-compatibility chunk and I did not score it.
Wire-chunk artifacts (profiles.rs, typescript035_models.rs, example, CHANGELOG/STABILITY/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES) were read only insofar as they evidence this chunk's claims.

Live/service acceptance for directional profiles remains explicitly unestablished (contracts/typescript-035-parity.json compatibility.liveAcceptance); I did not assess it, nor re-audit historical phase 19-24 infrastructure or release receipts.
